He played a key role in the early 17th-century Spanish diplomacy, particularly in the relations with the Catholic Church and the Habsburg Empire. Afán de Ribera was also involved in the governance of the Spanish Empire, overseeing the administration of various provinces in Europe and the Americas. He was a member of the Council of the Indies, a body responsible for governing the Spanish colonies in the New World. The Duke's diplomatic efforts were instrumental in shaping the Spanish foreign policy, and his legacy continued to influence Spanish politics and international relations for centuries. Afán de Ribera's diplomatic career was marked by several notable events, including the Treaty of Madrid with Portugal, which secured Spanish control over the Portuguese territories in South America. He also played a crucial role in the negotiations leading to the Treaty of Lisbon, which established the boundaries of the Spanish Netherlands. Afán de Ribera's involvement in the governance of the Spanish Empire was also significant, as he oversaw the administration of the provinces of Castile and Andalusia, which were crucial for the Spanish economy and military power. The Duke's diplomatic efforts and governance of the Spanish Empire had a lasting impact on Spanish history, shaping the country's relations with Europe and the Americas for centuries to come. His legacy is still remembered today, with his name evoking images of Spanish grandeur and diplomacy.

entities.summary: Fernando Afán de Ribera y Téllez-Girón, the duke of Alcalá de los Gazules, was a Spanish noble and diplomat who played a pivotal role in the early modern period of Spanish history. Born in Seville on May 10, 1583, he rose to prominence through his involvement in the Spanish Inquisition and his service as a royal advisor to King Philip III. Afán de Ribera's diplomatic efforts helped maintain the stability of the Spanish Empire, particularly in its relations with the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire. He died on March 28, 1637, in Madrid, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential figures in Spanish politics during the 17th century. His influence can be seen in the subsequent reigns of King Philip IV and the consolidation of the Spanish Habsburg dynasty. Afán de Ribera's story is a testament to the enduring power of the Spanish monarchy and the complex web of alliances that shaped the early modern world. Through his life and work, we can glimpse the intricate dance of politics, religion, and diplomacy that defined the era of the Spanish Golden Age.
